items.abstract: <jats:p>Accurately modeling user preferences is crucial for enhancing user experience in recommendation systems. However, current self-supervised learning methods heavily rely on high-quality data, limiting the diversity of user interest modeling and causing issues like data sparsity and popularity bias. This paper introduces Graph Transformer with Hard Negative Sample Supervised Contrastive Learning (HSCL-GT) to address these challenges. HSCL-GT enhances global information within the user-item interaction graph using Transformers, multi-head attention mechanisms and graph representation learning. It incorporates a hard negative sample contrastive learning strategy with a reinforced optimization loss function to improve recommendation signals. Comparative analyses against 12 established methods on datasets such as Yelp and LastFM reveal that HSCL-GT surpasses the GFormer method by 1.4% in Recall@20 and 2% in NDCG@20 on Yelp. Additionally, HSCL-GT significantly improves handling data sparsity and noise, demonstrating its potential for applications in e-commerce, social networking, video sharing and advertisement recommendations.</jats:p>
title: Transforming recommendation method based on contrastive learning with hard negative sampling
